poems: The kitchen's floor drain takes the last of the day.
1:01. The digits agree with each other.

Two hours of the new day gone.
Expenditures: none. Revenue: none.
The books balance.
A pizza box, closed, holding one slice, on the arm of a couch.

If I go under now, six hours.
If I finish this, five and a half.
I am negotiating with a person
who will not be me.
Last call was five minutes ago and nobody has moved.

Reheat instructions: microwave two minutes,
stir, one minute more.
Let stand.
Do not stand there in the door.

1:07 a.m. The router blinks its steady green,
traffic from the sleepless.
You have read the same paragraph three times. It is a good paragraph. It is not the problem.

I'm fine to drive.
You're not.
I'm fine to sit in the car.

A menu under the door
joins its brothers.
Bar mats up, wells wiped, one credit card still open behind the register with a stranger's name on it.

Ceiling fan.
Same four blades.
Same argument.
Dorm hallway. Someone's door propped with a shoe. Microwave popcorn, burnt an hour ago, still in the air.

1:14. The pillow flipped to the cool side,
a small country changing governments.

1:15. Two people at the stop,
betting on a schedule from memory.
A night nurse eats a sandwich standing up, one hand free for the call bell.
Second wind, n. The body overruling management.
Everyone left in the diner is either just starting or just ending. The coffee does not distinguish.
1:19. The building settles. It has been settling since 1974 and shows no sign of finishing.

1:20 a.m. The front door has not opened.
The house keeps its opinion.

1:21 a.m. One earbud in, one out:
half asleep, half company.

A hubcap in the gutter,
half full.

Take out the trash.
Set the machine.
Turn the deadbolt.
Do the small ones now.
Tomorrow invents its own.
Eleven time zones east, a man in a good shirt is deciding between the fish and the pasta.
1:25. Bad hour to text anyone. Excellent hour to draft it.
The ice cream sat out. It is a soup with a lid on it now.
Fry cook counts the hood filters. Six. Same as last week. Nobody has ever stolen a hood filter.
Everything closes but the parking lot.
New father, thirty minutes into a bottle, holding a head the size of a grapefruit and twice as serious.
1:30. Half the hour spent proving the other half will go the same way.

The train yard couples cars.
Two sounds,
a bang and then a longer bang.

Things still on:
the porch bulb,
the router,
the aquarium pump,
a laptop under a pillow,
an argument.
Somebody in the next apartment is doing the dishes at last. Good for them. Loud, though.
You said you would be up early. That was a different person, and they are not here to answer for it.

1:35 a.m. EXIT signs the only weather
on four empty floors.

A cat is running the length of the hall.
Twice. It is that hour.
Six hours, if the alarm is a suggestion.
Mop bucket wheeled out the back door, two wet stripes on the sidewalk going to the dumpster.

Text me when you get in.
You'll be out.
Text me anyway.
1:40 a.m. The gas station is lit like a stage and nobody has come to perform.
Highway sign says the airport is nine miles. At this hour the sign is telling the truth.
Freezer compressor kicks on. The house keeps going.
In the parking garage, a security guard reads a paperback with the cover folded back.
Tiredness arrived hours ago. Willingness is running late.
Quarter to two, and the pizza place kills its sign but keeps the oven warm for the crew.
Somebody is folding a futon back into a couch with the confidence of a person who has done it wrong before.
1:47. Nothing decided at this hour has ever survived contact with 8 a.m.

Grocery list, revised:
eggs
tape
the thing for the sink
whatever it was
ask

Hotel gym, one treadmill lit.
Her body is three time zones behind and gaining.
Ten to two. Somewhere a bar is playing its last song and everyone knows the words.

Refrigerator door open, held open,
the cold going out into the kitchen
while nothing is chosen.
A phone charger reaches the bed by four inches. Engineering has never solved this.
1:53. Every idea is brilliant. Write them down and see what you have made in the morning.
The dorm elevator goes up empty and comes back down empty and does it again.
A key, third try, then the good sound.
The last of the ice in the well melts down to water and the shift is over.

1:57 a.m. The night splits here:
the ones getting up soon, the ones not yet down.
Milk crate by the back door. A cook sits on it, not smoking, just sitting.

1:59. The pillow is interviewed
and gives nothing.
